newsitem.title: INDIA: Four killed in mob violence in west India--agency.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in mob violence in west India--agency.

text.p: Four people died and three others were seriously injured on Friday when police opened fire to disperse a mob in the western Indian state of Gujarat, the United News of India (UNI) news agency said.
The violence, linked to a continuing wave of tension between Hindu castes, erupted in Keshod town in Gujarat some 300 km (188 miles) southwest of the state capital of Gandhinagar, UNI said.

Police opened fire at an angry crowd trying to force shopkeepers to pull down their shutters in response to a general strike call given by upper caste groups. Lower-caste Hindus organised a similar protest strike on Wednesday.
The Keshod riot followed the deaths of 12 people when police opened fire to quell another mob on July 11 in the financial centre of Bombay in neighbouring Maharashtra state.
The Bombay unrest was triggered by the desecration of a statue of social activist B.R. Ambedkar, a leader of the lowest of Hindu castes, called Dalits.
